rawIngestions.titleRaw: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275$\times$ less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon

rawIngestions.titleRaw: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps. We introduce OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness organized around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory. The capability layer combines task-level tool interfaces with evidence rendering, providing consistent access to heterogeneous backends and converting their outputs into model-readable observations. Persistent multimodal memory retains the corresponding images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts throughout each query. A coding interface executes generated programs over stored data, enabling computations that combine results from multiple tools. Together, these mechanisms support an iterative process of acquiring, inspecting, and composing multimodal evidence. Evaluated on 22 benchmarks with eight open and proprietary backbones, OpenVLHarness improves average scores by 9.7-12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra. With GPT-6 Luna at medium reasoning effort, OpenVLHarness outperforms the base model, Codex, and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7-8.5 points while incurring at most 37% of their model-token cost.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
rawIngestions.contentRaw: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

payloadJson.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. However, the resulting corrections may conflate visual evidence with non-visual shifts induced by linguistic priors, response style, or the privileged view itself. We formalize this phenomenon as privileged-correction contamination: a token-level correction is contaminated when its update direction cannot be consistently attributed to the privileged visual evidence. Directly distilling contaminated corrections may therefore reinforce erroneous token-level updates. To address this issue, we propose reinforcement learning with visually attributable on-policy self-distillation, an evidence-consistent paradigm that augments task-level RLVR supervision with privileged token-level corrections grounded in visual evidence. We instantiate this paradigm with Visual-Attribution Gating (VAG), which uses the verifier-derived advantage as the optimization anchor and validates each privileged correction against the contrast between evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views. By admitting only corrections directionally supported by this visual contrast, VAG preserves visually grounded guidance while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Experiments across six visual reasoning benchmarks show that VAG consistently outperforms GRPO and OPSD methods, establishing new state-of-the-art average performance.

payloadJson.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation

rawIngestions.titleRaw: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.

payloadJson.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
rawIngestions.contentRaw: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. The five-axis metrics also distinguish systems with close public benchmark averages and show that high scores need not come with early or efficient gains. We study observational scaling from two perspectives: predicting the relative performance of VLM agents from their public capabilities, and forecasting later progress from early physical feedback. Together, these analyses ask how quickly and how far an agent can improve. Moreover, we conduct workspace interventions and then analyze what improvement leaves behind. Removing history reduces late-round success, frozen workspaces remain useful on unseen layouts, and three cross-task cases achieve success earlier. The results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.

payloadJson.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy

- Fixed subagents sometimes forgetting their most recent work when they were messaged or resumed right after finishing

- Fixed resumed and cloud sessions sending Claude the whole skill list again each time plugins reloaded at startup
- Fixed an interrupt not ending a Read that waits on an idle pipe or device named like an image

- Fixed a PreToolUse hook's deny reason being replaced by a timeout error when an Agent SDK callback hook on the same tool call timed out
- Fixed Bash and PowerShell deleting a large command's output file when it could not be copied to the session's tool-results folder, unless the disk is full
- Fixed notes typed into a multiple-choice question with previews being cut off with "…" in terminals under about 100 columns, hiding what was typed (anthropics/claude-code#82768)
- Fixed self-paced `/loop` wakeups scheduled at the 1-hour maximum firing just after the 1-hour prompt cache expired, so those wakeups no longer re-read the conversation uncached
- Fixed agent teams: approving a shutdown request from the main session no longer exits the whole CLI
- Fixed a skill's `once` hook also removing another skill's identical hook after it ran
- Fixed transcript mode's `{` and `}` landing the prompt on an inconsistent row, or off screen, instead of the transcript's first row
- Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200k` silently setting a 100K window: the variable now accepts `k` and `M` suffixes like `--autocompact`, and warns when a value is out of range or ignored
- Fixed Ctrl+C in the agents view clearing a text selection without copying it when pressed before the mouse button was released
- Improved `/usage` to say when a rate limit on usage data ends instead of "try again in a moment"
- Improved the lines shown when a mod written in the session loads, reloads or fails to load

- [VSCode] Fixed a session closed while it was starting keeping its Claude Code process running until the start ended
- [VSCode] Fixed a mod's drawings disappearing from a long-open panel until the next turn on machines that also run an older Claude Code
- [VSCode] Fixed Past conversations hiding sessions when `claudeCode.claudeProcessWrapper` is set
- [VSCode] Changed background sub-agents to show as one status line under their Agent card instead of streaming every step into the chat; the full transcript stays in /tasks
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed folders in the composer's @ list showing no name in cloud sessions, where picking one added only a space instead of a mention
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude going silent in a thread when its channel becomes shared across Enterprise Grid workspaces mid-task; it now posts a one-time note to @-mention it in a new thread
- [Claude Tag] Fixed `@Claude !fork` typed outside a thread getting no visible reply; Claude now shows you a private note saying to run it from inside a thread
- [Code Review] Added review levels to Code Review: Owners choose Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep for the organization, and can give individual repositories their own level
- [Code Review] Added an option in Code Review admin settings to review every repository in a GitHub organization, including ones added later, without selecting them one by one
- [Code Review] Fixed pull requests opened within a minute or two of an admin turning on Code Review being silently skipped; they are now retried and reviewed

- Fixed a "Prompt is too long" error when stopping a turn while the conversation was being compacted
- Fixed requests failing with "diagnostics: Extra inputs are not permitted" after switching to Vertex or Bedrock mid-session
- Fixed the Read tool loading an image file of any size, or a pipe or device named like an image, entirely into memory; image sources over 128 MB are now refused
- Fixed `/autocompact` and `/effort` saving to the wrong model when a gateway names Opus 4 or 4.1 with a prefix, such as `anthropic/claude-opus-4-1`
- Fixed a prompt cache miss when a tool added mid-session was loaded again through ToolSearch or after compaction
- Fixed `claude plugin` and other subcommands sometimes exiting before a queued settings or config write finished, which could lose the change or leave a `.tmp` file behind
- Fixed plugin marketplaces re-cloning on every refresh, and newly installed git plugins showing version "unknown", when git defaults to the reftable ref format
- Fixed the PowerShell tool not finding commands in a plugin's `bin/` folder, and reporting an error when a search that finds nothing (rg, grep, findstr, git grep) is piped into `Select-Object` or another formatting cmdlet
- Fixed Claude in the desktop app pointing you to claude.ai settings or `/mcp` to authorize or reconnect an MCP server where that option isn't available
- Fixed artifact publishes sometimes failing when Claude sent an empty list of edits, and Claude retrying an artifact update the wrong way after a newer version of the artifact turned it away
- Fixed `classifier_category` missing from OpenTelemetry `tool_decision` events for most auto mode classifier blocks, and new `tool_decision` attributes pushing out `tool_use_id`, `tool_source` and `tool_parameters` when `OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT` is low
- Fixed rows in the agents view staying blank after moving down a long list or folding a section
- Fixed `claude remote-control --help` not printing its usage and exiting when not signed in
- Fixed `/design consent` and `/design revoke` suggesting `/design-login` when they fail in a cloud session, where it isn't available; the message now points to claude.ai/design/settings

- Fixed a cloud session's cost and usage restarting from zero after the session resumed in a new process

- Improved the message when a background session reopened from another folder has no LLM gateway: it now says why, instead of "Not logged in"

- Changed prompt and agent hooks so that at most 12 of one event run at a time; the rest wait their turn
- Changed the message shown when your organization's policy turns off `/feedback`: it now points to GitHub issues instead of an organization admin
- [VSCode] Fixed text after an unclosed code block in a list showing as plain text while a reply streams, then turning into code
- [VSCode] Fixed MCP server sign-in from the panel opening a broken authorization page when the server URL contains a query string
- [VSCode] Fixed the `@browser` banner saying "Browser connected" when no browser with the Claude extension can be reached
- [Cloud sessions] Added a banner on a routine's page that says why its last run didn't start, such as your organization reaching its limit on concurrent cloud sessions
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed "Rewind to here" failing on every message except the newest in cloud sessions; self-hosted runners need Claude Code v2.1.246 or later
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the pull request status bar in cloud sessions flipping a pull request with merge conflicts back to ready while GitHub rechecked it
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed routine runs showing as Completed after their cloud session stopped unexpectedly, and as Cancelled when archived before they started, instead of failed
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the diff view in cloud sessions missing changes or failing to load after the session's GitHub repository was renamed or moved
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed a scheduled routine run that failed partway being run again from the start an hour or more later, which could repeat work such as posting the same report twice
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed an open cloud session sometimes not showing messages sent from another device until you reloaded the page or clicked away and back
- [Cloud sessions] Improved the error shown when a cloud session fails to start: it now says "Connection lost" or "Server error" instead of "Something went wrong"
- [Remote Control] Fixed a subagent's pane spinning forever in a Remote Control session after your computer goes offline; it now says Remote Control is disconnected
- [Claude Tag] Fixed "is thinking…" staying up under a mention in a Slack channel or DM after Claude answered it by editing one of its earlier messages
- [Claude Tag] Fixed URLs in code blocks under a numbered or bulleted step of Claude's Slack replies being wrapped in angle brackets, which broke copied commands
- [Claude Tag] Fixed HEIC, SVG, TIFF and BMP images attached in Slack never reaching Claude; they now arrive as files in its working files, like other file types
- [Claude Tag] Fixed new channel managers losing access to Claude in Slack in organizations that restrict Claude Tag by role; the manager role now also grants Claude Tag in Slack
- [Claude Tag] Fixed custom connectors whose MCP servers share one host showing as a single connector in Claude Tag admin settings; each server is now its own connector
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack sometimes answering a direct message with "DMs are temporarily unavailable" and dropping it when a single Slack lookup stalled; it now retries first
- [Claude Tag] Fixed direct messages with Claude on a Slack Enterprise Grid ignoring Slack's workspace dropdown; they now run under the connected workspace you last opened Claude in
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack's notice for a channel's monthly spend limit saying a channel manager can raise it; it now names an organization owner and links the usage page
- [Claude Tag] Fixed links in Claude's Slack replies absorbing the closing bold or italic marks, or full-width punctuation, right after them, which broke the link and the formatting
- [Claude Tag] Improved repository search in Claude Tag admin settings to cover up to 100 connected GitHub accounts and find private repositories past the first 5,000 of a GitHub App install
- [Claude Tag] Improved Add place in Claude Tag admin settings to list a channel you type or paste right away, instead of only after your organization's full channel list has loaded
- [Claude Tag] Improved Add > Domain on a workspace's or channel's page in Claude Tag admin settings to be available once that page loads, not only after every channel has loaded
- [Claude Tag] Changed Claude Tag admin settings to organize Claude's access into four tabs: Bundles, Connectors, Skills and plugins, and Channels
- [Claude Tag] Changed the Roles page in organization settings to group the roles created for Claude Tag channel managers in a collapsed section below your organization's own roles
- [Code Review] Fixed Code Review setup not resuming after you leave to connect GitHub; back in admin settings, it now reopens at the repository picker

rawIngestions.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.301 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_MAX_USAGE_LIMIT_WAIT_MS` so unattended retry mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`) ends a request at a usage limit that resets too far away instead of waiting
- Added OpenTelemetry tracing guidance to the `claude-api` skill, including setting up trace destinations with the `ant` CLI
- Added the `%` motion to vim mode: jump to the matching bracket, alone or with d/c/y
- Added `rows` to a mod's `Input`: a text field of several lines in the terminal, where Enter submits and Shift+Enter or a backslash before Enter starts a new line
- Added `classifier_verdict` and `permission_mode` to OpenTelemetry `tool_decision` events, so auto mode classifier decisions can be told apart from permission rules
- Added `classifier_category` to OpenTelemetry `tool_decision` events, naming the built-in rule a classifier block matched, when `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1`
- Fixed quitting removing a worktree made by a `WorktreeCreate` hook without asking when it may hold unpushed commits
- Fixed the `fable` (and `best`) model alias erroring on the Anthropic API when the newest Fable model is not available to your organization: Claude Code now retries once on the previous Fable model
- Fixed a misleading "Please run /login" error when a full disk keeps the login from being refreshed; the error now names the disk and says to delete files
- Fixed Grep and Glob reporting no matches when the search program failed unexpectedly before returning any results; they now return an error saying the search failed
- Fixed workflow agents sometimes skipping their step, and the run still reporting success, after reading the harness note that their task text carries no user authority
- Fixed artifact updates being refused where a PreToolUse hook covers Edit or Write; Claude now edits the file and then republishes instead of changing it in the publish call
- Fixed skills and commands with very many or very long argument names stalling for seconds when invoked; only the first 64 names, each up to 64 characters, are now filled in
- Fixed skills, commands and hooks using very large amounts of memory when their arguments fill many placeholders
- Fixed stray characters such as `>0q` covering the folder trust prompt, and `>4m` before the shell prompt at exit, in terminals built on VTE older than 0.53 such as MATE Terminal on RHEL 8
- Fixed stray `GOK` text appearing in the prompt at startup in some versions of iTerm2
- Fixed switching to a model whose name contains `application-inference-profile` running your `awsAuthRefresh` command and delaying model-switch hooks when the provider is not Bedrock
- Fixed sign-in refresh timeouts and unexpected sign-outs after a short command such as `claude auth status` or `claude plugin list` exited in the middle of a token refresh
- Fixed a tool call cut off by a message sent mid-turn during its permission check being reported to the model as rejected by the user
- Fixed a case where switching to a model with a smaller context window could spend usage credits on a summary by the previous model without asking first
- Fixed conversations being compacted over and over, on a model you didn't pick, behind an LLM gateway whose responses name a different model than the one requested
- Fixed vim mode sometimes staying in INSERT after Escape on a slow or busy machine
- Fixed Esc discarding a typed AskUserQuestion answer in vim mode: the free-text field now supports vim NORMAL mode, and Esc cancels only from NORMAL
- Fixed the Read tool reading binary files such as .xlsm, .parquet, .epub and .heic as text
- Fixed a Markdown table with only a header row drawing nothing when too wide for the terminal, including in plans on the plan approval card
- Fixed the /claude-api skill saying CMEK external-key endpoints aren't available on Claude Platform on AWS
- Fixed skills no longer being listed to the model after using `/rewind`
- Fixed the compaction row in a resumed session offering ctrl+o for history that is not loaded; it now says where the earlier messages are saved, and also shows in fullscreen
- Fixed the "new task? /clear to save tokens" hint coming back right after you interrupt a response
- Fixed the permission prompt for a plugin or skill hook's `ask` decision not showing which plugin or skill the hook comes from
- Fixed `/diff` not noticing a conflicted cherry-pick or revert in reftable repositories when one of its git checks timed out or failed
- Fixed workflow scripts asking for permission or being refused when read, edited or re-run after a Bash `cd` in the same session
- Fixed dim text on the dark ANSI theme and 16-color terminals: faint inside filled boxes, not faint under selection and search highlights, and list descriptions dimmed like other secondary text
- Fixed a mod's `$.model.fork` returning `nothing-to-fork` when called before the first response of a new Claude Code process had finished, as in `claude -p` runs and cloud sessions
- Fullscreen mode: Fixed `/compact` and auto-compact briefly freezing the UI while the visible transcript is rebuilt
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions started from Slack being unable to find or attach a repository when managed settings restrict MCP servers; use `deniedMcpServers` to keep those tools off
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions being reported as having a deleted source branch, and not retried, when an unrelated setup or session failure quoted git's missing-ref wording
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed the log promising a retry of a failed or declined session release for a session that is ending; repeated failures now show a count
- Windows: Fixed stopped background PowerShell commands missing the closing `[killed]` line in their output file
- Improved switching to a model with a smaller context window: a conversation too long for the new model is now summarized by the previous model first
- Improved rendering performance while a long-running subagent works: its progress trail now updates incrementally instead of being reprocessed in full on every render
- Improved artifacts: pages Claude writes now paint the band above a sticky header, so scrolled text no longer shows there in the mobile apps
- Improved mods: in VS Code and the desktop and mobile apps, a tree drawn above the question dialog can now hold Markdown and up to 48 rows; the terminal keeps 12 plain rows
- Changed a mod hook's `.catch` handler to run only when the hook throws or times out; events raised beneath the hook's own calls now skip that hook without asking its `.catch`
- Changed a mod's `$.env.set` to resolve with `{}` once the variable is set or unset, or with `{ deny }` saying why when the write is not made
- [VSCode] Added LaTeX math rendering in Claude's responses, including `$$` and multi-line `\[ … \]` blocks and inline `$…$` and `\(…\)` math

- Fixed workflow agents sometimes skipping their step, and the run still reporting success, after reading the harness note that their task text carries no user authority
- Fixed artifact updates being refused where a PreToolUse hook covers Edit or Write; Claude now edits the file and then republishes instead of changing it in the publish call
- Fixed skills and commands with very many or very long argument names stalling for seconds when invoked; only the first 64 names, each up to 64 characters, are now filled in

- Fixed stray characters such as `>0q` covering the folder trust prompt, and `>4m` before the shell prompt at exit, in terminals built on VTE older than 0.53 such as MATE Terminal on RHEL 8

- Fixed sign-in refresh timeouts and unexpected sign-outs after a short command such as `claude auth status` or `claude plugin list` exited in the middle of a token refresh

rawIngestions.titleRaw: huggingface/transformers v5.20.0 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. Pipelines get a cleanup of generation-argument handling that removes spurious warnings. * Add job to automatically generate Intel CPU Docker image (#49560) by @regisss in [#49560] * Image decoding moves to torchcodec (#47963) by @zucchini-nlp in [#47963] * Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync (#49426) by @tengomucho in [#49426] * Generation cleanup in pipelines (#49269) by @Rocketknight1 in [#49269] * Fix Whisper batch timestamp decoding for tensors (#49419) by @Kingofbooks in [#49419] ## Vision Vision processing was updated in several places. release.body: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. ## NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super

[NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-super) is a vision-language model for coding, reasoning, tool use, and document understanding. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer mixture-of-experts backbone (12B active per token) with a C-RADIO vision encoder, and supports tool calling, an on/off thinking mode, and context up to 1M tokens.

```
ollama run nemotron-3.5-super
```

A compact sibling, [Nemotron 3.5 Bolt](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-bolt), distills Super down to 74B parameters (9B active) tuned to fit a 24 GB NVIDIA GPU for everyday agentic tasks, with speculative decoding via its included drafter.

## What's Changed
* Decision models are now available on cloud — use `clef:cloud` and `clef-flash:cloud` to run decision models through ollama.com cloud without pulling them locally
* Continuing an OpenAI-compatible Responses conversation that includes custom tool calls no longer fails with an error
* Clearer error messages when cloud access fails: sign-in problems, payment issues in the desktop app, and upstream access errors from the ChatGPT gateway now explain what went wrong
* Updated llama.cpp (adding Nemotron 3.5 support) and MLX

When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: Elf0 – Build and run AI agent workflows in YAML (CLI)
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hi HN — I built Elf0, a command-line tool to define and run AI agent workflows in YAML. It helps you iterate on small multi-step "agents" without scaffolding a whole codebase.

The agent patterns described in Anthropic's article was an inspiration: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-age... I then used Nvidia's AgentIQ YAML spec as inspiration.

Why: I keep bumping into tasks where a single prompt isn’t enough (e.g., extracting quote data from an insurance PDF). Defining the workflow in YAML makes it easy to version prompts, parameters and logic, and to feed the whole spec back to an LLM to improve.

What it does: - Run single- or multi-step agents from a YAML spec. - Reference files or directories in prompts with @file / @dir. - Improve a workflow with a built-in command. - Use OpenAI or Anthropic APIs, or run locally via Ollama. - Optional MCP server example (YouTube transcript analyser). - Interactive mode for step-by-step runs.

Anyway it's been a lot of fun and really useful, let me know any ideas you might have to improve it?

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
